## Brief
Objective: make test/profiles-route.test.js pass on Windows. Cascade (07) diagnosed it: line 101, `assert.match(robots, /^User-agent: \*\nAllow: \/$/m, 'everything is allowed')`, joins two lines with a literal `\n`, which rejects the CRLF checkout the windows-latest runner produces for web/robots.txt (PR #348, run 34926833483, the only failure of 1671 tests). The house pattern is `\r?\n` (src/packs.js:25, scripts/dev-env.js:60, scripts/start-local.js:44).

Change: in that regex, `\n` becomes `\r?\n`, and check every other assertion in the same test (and the file) for the same shape: any regex or string comparison that spans a line break, or anchors `$` before an embedded newline, must accept `\r?`. Nothing else changes; web/robots.txt, scripts/build-web.js, .gitattributes and test/build-web.test.js stay as they are.

Proof, both quoted in `member result`: `node --test test/profiles-route.test.js` passes; and a node one-liner that reads web/robots.txt, converts it to CRLF (`.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`), and applies every changed regex to it, printing true for each.
Deliverables: test/profiles-route.test.js only, in /Users/ericlugo/Personal/BadTakes/.claude/worktrees/bad-015-public-profiles on branch feat/bad-015-profiles-route. Leave the change uncommitted; Spud commits.
